sections.html:
Kingman sellers in a hurry usually choose between an agent listing and a direct sale to a cash buyer. The paperwork is the same either way. Kingman is the seat of Mohave County, so the recorder, the assessor, the treasurer and the courts sit within a few blocks of each other downtown.

A listing reaches the widest group of buyers but leans on showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal. A cash sale usually skips the loan and the appraisal, which shortens the calendar, though the offer reflects the buyer taking on repairs and risk. Whichever route you pick, gather these first:

  • Your recorded deed and the Mohave County parcel number
  • Payoff figures for any mortgage, home equity line or lien
  • Permit records for work done on the house
  • HOA or special district contacts, if the lot has any
  • The most recent property tax bill

Kingman has an estimated 35,829 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 9.6 percent from the April 2020 base. Owners occupy 68.4 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied home is worth $267,700, and median gross rent is $1,058. There are 15,206 households of 2.20 people, and the median household income is $61,792. Treat the median as a rough anchor and ask a local agent or appraiser what comparable sales look like now.

The city covers about 37.5 square miles at roughly 3,471 feet, where Interstate 40 and U.S. 93 meet. Summer highs rarely pass 107 degrees, winter nights often drop below freezing, snow is possible, and yearly precipitation is about 8 inches. A buyer's inspector will study the heating system, pipe insulation and roof as closely as the air conditioner.

Work done without a permit is the item most likely to slow a Kingman sale. The Building Division of Development Services takes applications for residential, commercial, industrial, demolition and signage work. Call (928) 753-8130 to ask about an address before you list. The division also publishes a residential permit process guide that explains the Minor Improvement Permit for smaller jobs.

Inspections are scheduled by phone. The city wants the request in before 7:00 a.m. on the day you want the inspector, with your permit number and job site address ready. If a patio cover, room addition or garage conversion was built years ago, ask what the city has on file and what a retroactive permit would take. Fixing that before an offer arrives avoids a renegotiation at inspection.

Houses outside the city in unincorporated Mohave County can fall under a different rule. A.R.S. 33-422 covers a seller of five or fewer parcels of land, other than subdivided land, in an unincorporated area. The seller gives the buyer a written affidavit of disclosure at least seven days before transfer, and the buyer has a five-day rescission right.

Short-term rentals inside city limits need a city permit under Ordinance No. 1952, effective October 1, 2023. The requirements are a $60 annual fee, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, a 24-hour emergency contact and written notice to neighboring homes. Operating without a permit can bring fines of up to $1,000 a month. Arizona law at A.R.S. 9-500.39 limits how far a city may restrict these rentals, but a permit is allowed.

A buyer who plans to rent by the night will ask whether your property has a permit, so be ready to answer yes or no.

The Mohave County Treasurer bills property tax in two installments.

InstallmentDuePast due after
First halfOctober 15:00 p.m., November 1
Second halfMarch 15:00 p.m., May 1

A weekend November 1 moves the first-half date to the next business day. Bills over $100 paid in one payment by December 31 owe no interest accrued after November 1. Late payments carry 16 percent annual interest, prorated monthly.

Ask the escrow officer how the current year's tax will be prorated at closing. If a bill reaches you after the sale, forward it to the new owner or return it to P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with a note about the sale. The Assessor at 928-753-0703 can confirm the sale was recorded.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Mohave County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Mohave County Recorder, 700 West Beale Street in Kingman, which lists a $30 fee for recording documents. Arizona law requires an Affidavit of Property Value to be attached to a deed that transfers title, unless the deed carries an exemption notation (A.R.S. 11-1133), and the recorder refuses a deed without one. Your title or escrow company normally prepares both. Staff cannot advise on how to fill out forms.

The recorder's self-service search shows recorded liens by name, but a search alone does not prove the property is clear, so buyers rely on title insurance. Copies of a recorded deed cost $1.00 per page.

sections.h2: Who buys Kingman houses that need work
sections.html:
Investors and cash buyers are the usual buyers for Kingman houses with deferred repairs, tenants in place, an inherited title or a looming payment problem. They price the work and the time into their offer, so expect a number below a fully repaired retail sale in exchange for speed and fewer conditions.

Compare offers on net proceeds. Ask each buyer who pays escrow and title charges, how long the buyer needs to close, whether the buyer will accept the house as is and what happens to the deposit if the buyer backs out. Get the offer in writing and read the contract before you sign. If you are behind on a mortgage, ask your lender for a payoff figure and the sale deadline first, since the calendar sets your options.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Kingman house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, you can offer the house as is. A buyer using a loan may ask for repairs after an appraisal or inspection, while investors and cash buyers often accept a house in its current condition. Open permits and unpermitted additions can still delay closing, so call Development Services at (928) 753-8130 to check your address.

faqs.q: How long does recording a deed take in Mohave County?
faqs.a: The recorder checks each document against the recording requirements in A.R.S. 11-480 and, if it is complete and the fee is paid, assigns a recording number. Mailed originals come back in about 4 to 6 weeks, while in-person documents are returned after scanning.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax if I sell in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: Ask your escrow officer how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer. Mohave County bills are due October 1 and March 1, with the first half past due after November 1. The settlement statement should show the split.
Yes, with a permit. The city requires a permit, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, an emergency contact and neighbor notice for rentals under 30 days inside city limits. The annual fee is $60.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a lien or a title question on a Kingman property?
faqs.a: Start with a title company, because the recorder's staff cannot give legal advice or do research for you. The Mohave County Recorder at (928) 753-0701 can show you how to run a basic search by name, and a title company can tell you whether liens or judgments will cut into your proceeds.
